scenes.text: Have you ever had a long chat with ChatGPT, and it forgot what you said at the start? [1] That's not a bug. It's because of tokens, and something called the context window. [2] So let's break it down.

title: Tokens &
Context
data.subtitle: Why AI forgets in long chats

scenes.text: L L Ms don't read words the way we do. [1] They read tokens, which are small chunks of text, often a whole word, or just a part of a word. [2] Common words are usually one token, [3] rare words get split into pieces, [4] and numbers and symbols count as tokens too.

data.definition: A small chunk of text, a word or a piece of a word, that the model reads.

scenes.text: Here's how it looks. [1] A long word like unbelievable can be split into pieces, like un, believ, and able. [2] As a rough rule, one token is about three quarters of a word, [3] so a hundred tokens is about seventy five words. [4] And here's why it matters, AI companies charge you per token.

Now, let's talk about the context window. [1] Think of it as the model's working memory. Your messages and its replies all have to fit inside it. So when the chat gets too long, [2] the oldest messages fall out, and the model simply forgets them.

data.heading: The context window
data.label: WINDOW: 6 MESSAGES
messages: Sorry, I don't know your name.
data.note: Too long? The oldest messages drop out.

scenes.text: And the good news is, these windows keep growing. [1] Early chatbots could hold only a few pages of text. [2] But modern models can hold hundreds of thousands of tokens, that's entire books, all at once.

So why should you care? [1] First, cost, because more tokens means a bigger bill. [2] Second, long documents sometimes need to be split into smaller chunks. [3] And third, in a long chat, when the AI starts forgetting, just start a fresh chat, or ask it for a summary.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think the AI remembers everything they've ever told it. [2] It doesn't. It only sees what fits in the current context window. Those memory features just quietly add a few saved notes into your prompt.

data.myth: The AI remembers everything I ever told it.
data.fact: It only sees what fits in the context window. 'Memory' features just add saved notes to your prompt.
data.tip: Long chat acting weird? Start fresh.

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] AI reads text as tokens. [2] One token is about three quarters of a word. [3] The context window is its working memory, [4] and when the chat gets too long, old messages fall out.
